source_text:
Ὁρᾷς ἐν ἀρχῇ τὴν ὁμολογίαν, ἤγουν τὴν ἀνάρρησιν· τὸ μὲν γὰρ εἶ τέθεικεν,
ἵνα δείξῃ τὸ προαιώνιον· οὐ γὰρ ἐν χρόνῳ γέγονεν, ἀλλ' ἦν ἀεὶ τοῦτο, τουτέστιν
υἱός. ἐπήνεγκε δὲ τό Σήμερον ἐγέννησά σε, ἵνα τὴν νεωτάτην αὐτοῦ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα
δείξῃ γέννησιν, ἣν ὑπέμεινεν ἑκὼν διὰ τῆς ἁγίας Παρθένου. ταύτῃ τοι καὶ Θεοτόκος
ὠνόμασται· τέτοκε γὰρ οὐκ ἄνθρωπον ἁπλῶς κατά γε τὴν ἔξωθεν σχέσιν
συναφθέντα τῷ Θεῷ, αὐτὸν δὲ μᾶλλον τὸν ἐκ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς Λόγον τὴν ἀνθρώπειαν
ὑποδύντα πτωχείαν καὶ γενόμενον καθ' ἡμᾶς ἄνθρωπον.
thought_title: The Father's twofold begetting of the Son
orientation: Cyril is explaining how the Father's words in Psalm 2:7 reveal both the Son's eternal existence and his birth in the flesh from the Virgin.
pass_a_gloss: You see in the beginning the confession, that is the declaration; for the 'you are' he has set, in order that he might show the eternal; for not in time did it come to be, but he was always this, that is Son. And he brought in the 'Today I have begotten you,' in order that he might show his newest and according to the flesh birth, which he underwent willingly through the holy Virgin. For this reason indeed she has been named Mother of God; for she has given birth not to a human being simply, according at least to the outward relation, joined to God, but rather to the very Word from God the Father, who put on human poverty and became a human being like us.

choices.term: Ὁρᾷς ἐν ἀρχῇ τὴν ὁμολογίαν, ἤγουν τὴν ἀνάρρησιν
choices.english: You see in the beginning the confession, that is the declaration
choices.why: Keeps the second-person address and the explanatory 'that is' for ἤγουν; 'confession' and 'declaration' preserve the two distinct nouns without merging them.
rejected: You see at the start the acknowledgment, namely the proclamation

choices.english: for the 'you are' he has set
choices.why: Preserves the perfect tense of τέθεικεν and the quoted 'you are' as the object; the word order mirrors the Greek emphasis on the quoted phrase.
rejected: for he has placed the 'you are'

choices.term: τὴν νεωτάτην αὐτοῦ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα δείξῃ γέννησιν
choices.english: his newest and according to the flesh birth
choices.why: Keeps the superlative νεωτάτην as 'newest' and the adverbial κατὰ σάρκα as 'according to the flesh,' matching the glossary's 'flesh' for σάρξ.
rejected: his most recent birth in the flesh

choices.english: she has been named Mother of God
choices.why: Uses the glossary English 'Mother of God' for Θεοτόκος and keeps the perfect passive 'has been named.'
Keeps the aorist participle 'who put on' and the literal 'human poverty' for ἀνθρώπειαν πτωχείαν, preserving the metaphor of clothing.

choices.english: became a human being like us
choices.why: Renders καθ' ἡμᾶς as 'like us' and keeps 'human being' for ἄνθρωπον, distinguishing it from 'flesh' (σάρξ).
rejected: became a human as we are

pass_b_english: Cyril says: You see the confession at the very start, that is, the declaration. For the Father has set down the words "You are" in order to show the Son's eternal being. He did not become Son in time; he always was this—that is, Son. Then the Father brought in the words "Today I have begotten you" (Psalm 2:7) in order to show his newest birth according to the flesh, which he willingly underwent through the holy Virgin. This is why she has been named Mother of God. For she gave birth not to a mere human being simply joined to God by an external connection, but rather to the very Word from God the Father, who put on human poverty and became a human being like us.

problems.quote: joined to God in some outward relation
problems.why: Missing 'simply'/'merely' (ἁπλῶς) and 'according to' (κατά γε τὴν ἔξωθεν σχέσιν); 'outward relation' alone loses the 'external connection' sense.
problems.fix: a mere human being simply joined to God by an external connection
problems.ruling: ἁπλῶς ('simply') and κατά γε τὴν ἔξωθεν σχέσιν ('according to outward relation') are dropped, altering the theological nuance.

edits.old: not to a mere human being joined to God in some outward relation
edits.new: not to a mere human being simply joined to God by an external connection

problems.source_quote: τὴν νεωτάτην αὐτοῦ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα δείξῃ γέννησιν
problems.why: Glossary requires 'flesh' for σάρξ; 'newest birth' omits 'flesh' entirely.
problems.fix: his newest birth according to the flesh
problems.ruling: Source says κατὰ σάρκα ('according to flesh'); English 'newest birth' omits 'flesh,' losing incarnational meaning.

edits.old: in order to show his newest birth, the one according to the flesh
edits.new: in order to show his newest birth according to the flesh

fixed: The glossary issue about 'newest birth' omitting 'flesh' is real; the English has been adjusted to 'his newest birth according to the flesh'.

problems.quote: You see the confession at the very start
problems.why: Unclear who speaks: Cyril addressing reader, or Father's voice?

problems.quote: his newest birth according to the flesh
problems.why: 'Newest' is odd English; suggests comparison where none exists.
Likely means 'human condition/lowliness' not economic poverty.
problems.fix: Use 'human lowliness' or gloss the phrase.

problems.quote: his newest birth according to the flesh
problems.why: 'Newest' does not fit patristic usage; likely translates a Greek word meaning 'recent' or 'latter.'
problems.fix: Use 'recent' or 'latter' birth to contrast with eternal generation.

edits.old: You see the confession at the very start
edits.new: Cyril says: You see the confession at the very start

edits.old: his newest birth according to the flesh
edits.new: his recent birth according to the flesh

fixed: Changed 'newest' to 'recent' to avoid implying comparison and to reflect the Greek νεωτάτην as 'recent/latter' in contrast to eternal generation.
Changed 'human poverty' to 'human lowliness' to avoid economic connotation and reflect ἀνθρώπειαν πτωχείαν as the humble human condition.
Added 'Cyril says:' to clarify the speaker as Cyril addressing the reader.

problems.quote: Cyril says: You see the confession
problems.why: Unclear if Cyril speaks or quotes someone; 'confession at the very start' of what?
problems.fix: Clarify Cyril comments on Psalm 2:7's opening words.

problems.why: Unclear what this opposes; likely 'external conjunction' or 'mere association'.
problems.fix: Use 'mere external union' or gloss as Nestorian view.

problems.quote: Cyril says: You see the confession at the very start
problems.why: Unclear whether 'Cyril says' introduces Cyril's own voice or a later compiler's attribution.
problems.fix: Clarify: this is Cyril's own commentary voice continuing.

edits.old: Cyril says: You see the confession at the very start, that is, the declaration.
edits.new: You see the confession at the very start, that is, the declaration.

fixed: The speaker problem is resolved by removing the editorial 'Cyril says:' so the commentary voice is Cyril's own, matching the source's direct address.
The mistranslation is fixed by rendering 'κατά γε τὴν ἔξωθεν σχέσιν συναφθέντα' as 'by a mere external union', which better conveys the contrast with the Word's true incarnation.

last_rejected.why: 'νεωτάτην' means 'most recent/latest', not 'newest' which implies best/renewed.
last_rejected.ruling: νεωτάτην is superlative of νέος; 'newest' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'σάρξ' as 'flesh'; 'πτωχείαν' here means humble condition of human flesh.
last_rejected.ruling: πτωχείαν means 'poverty'; 'human poverty' renders ἀνθρώπειαν πτωχείαν accurately, no glossary issue.
